subject: Post-call: Security posture & private deployment topology — evidence and next steps
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Security posture & private deployment topology — evidence and next steps

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and action items from our end after the discovery call. High-level notes: 

- MindWell is evaluating a private deployment (VPC or on-prem) to meet HIPAA and internal data governance controls.
- Main concerns flagged: SOC 2 status, audit logs retention, network isolation (air-gapped vs VPC peering), key management, and procurement timeline.

Action items (Redwood):
- Share a concise vendor RFI template you can forward to procurement (attached).
- Provide our minimal evidence checklist for SOC / HIPAA-required controls and our recommended topology options (VPC peering, S2S VPN, and a fully air-gapped model).
- Ask: can you share an annotated network sketch showing where your data plane and EHR connectors live (subnets, NAT, egress points)? That will let us scope routing and egress allowlist work.

Attachments: vendor-rfi-template.docx (Redwood RFI template), sample evidence matrix.

Questions for you: 
1) Do you have a required timeline for SOC 2 Type II or a deadline for managed service onboarding?
2) Is there a strict airgap requirement (no outbound connectivity from the inference hosts) or would a tightly controlled egress allowlist suffice for your use case?
3) Who on your side will own the annotated diagram (network/security architect) so we can loop them into the follow-up?

Proposed next step: annotated diagram + completed RFI draft from MindWell by end of next week, then a short 30-min tech sync to align on topology and evidence.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the Drive links and our evidence checklist in a separate note.

—
Rohan Mehta
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rohan_mehta@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call: Security posture & private deployment topology — evidence and next steps

Thanks Rohan — great summary. Quick answers inline and an initial upload: I've attached a rough network sketch (mindwell-network-sketch.vsdx).

- SOC 2: Completed Type I (June 2025). Type II audit fieldwork is in progress with a vendor; target completion Q3 2027. We can share the SysTrust report extract and our control mapping.
- HIPAA/GDPR: We are HIPAA-covered; GDPR applies to EU patient subsets — we have a DPA template and regional-data routing in place.
- Airgap requirement: For core PHI pipelines we prefer no direct outbound internet from inference hosts (airlock / egress-controlled). Some non-PHI models could tolerate egress allowlist.
- Key management: We use a customer-managed KMS (Azure Key Vault) for production keys; dev uses a separate KMS instance.

Questions for Redwood:
- What minimal log retention window do you need to demonstrate for HIPAA requests?
- For a VPC-peered deployment, do you support both AWS and Azure peering patterns?

I’ll try to get an annotated diagram from our infra lead (cc’d: security_ops@cloudprime.com — they are our SRE partner) and a first-pass procurement contact by Friday.

—
Samantha Li
Director, Product & Privacy — MindWell Health
samantha.li@mindwellhealth.com
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@mindwellhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Security posture & private deployment topology — evidence and next steps

Appreciate the quick replies and the sketch — that helps a lot. A few clarifications and concrete asks below (inline with your points):

- SOC 2 / evidence: Our minimal evidence set for HIPAA/SOC spot-checks is: SOC summary, network diagram (annotated), KMS architecture, access control list for service accounts, and sample audit logs (last 90 days). For formal Type II acceptance we typically map controls to your SOC report; we can prepare that mapping if you share the current Type I report and audit schedule.

- Airgap vs egress allowlist: We support three production patterns:
  * Full airlock: inference hosts have no outbound internet; updates come via an approved artifact sync process.
  * Egress-allowlist: outbound to a small set of Redwood-managed endpoints (TLS-only) + IP ranges; this supports streaming and monitoring.
  * Hybrid: segregate PHI workloads onto airlocked hosts and non-PHI on allowlist hosts.

- Cloud support: we support VPC peering and private link patterns for AWS and Azure. For Azure we recommend Private Link over peering for cross-subscription isolation.

Action items for MindWell (ask):
- Please upload an annotated network diagram that marks: where PHI is stored, inference host subnet(s), NAT/egress points, firewall zones, and any 3rd-party connectors. (Attachment we received: mindwell-network-sketch.vsdx — useful but needs more annotations.)
- Provide your procurement point-of-contact and any required SLAs / contract redlines so Redwood can prepare a draft.

Deliverables from Redwood (by EOW):
- Completed vendor RFI template (attached) and an evidence checklist PDF.
- A short topology options document showing tradeoffs: latency, ops complexity, and egress constraints.

I’ve attached the vendor-rfi-template.docx. I’ll also share a Drive folder with the evidence checklist and a sample annotated diagram. If you can get us the annotated diagram by next Friday, we’ll schedule a 30-min tech sync the following week.

On the log-retention question: our compliance baseline expects searchable audit logs for 90 days and immutable archival for 1 year by default; we can extend that if you have longer retention requirements tied to legal/regulatory needs.

Thanks — looping Lauren to coordinate the tech sync cadence.
